about.description: {{appName}} keeps your notes, checklists, money and health in one simple place, so you can just write it down and find it again.

features.title: What it does
features.description: Notes that format themselves as you type, checklists you can share with your household, finance books in any currency with charts and category suggestions, and health logs for the whole family, from weight and blood sugar to a child's growth and periods.

private.title: Private by design
private.description: Your items are end-to-end encrypted on your device, so only you and the people you share with can read them; not even we can. Category suggestions are worked out on your device too. Your data is never sold or used for advertising.

everywhere.title: Wherever you are
everywhere.description: It works in any browser on your phone or computer, installs like an app and opens even when you are offline. Choose light or dark, a text size, and English or Bahasa Indonesia.

made.title: Who makes it
made.description: Made by <portfolio>{{author}}</portfolio>. It is free, and its <github>source code</github> is open on GitHub. See what is new in the <changelog>changelog</changelog>.

help.description: A short guide to everything Catat Saja does, and where to find it.

start.title: Getting started
start.description: Create an account, then use the menu to move between Notes, Tasks, Finances and Health.
steps: Sign up with your email and a password (then open the link in the verification email), or sign in with Google.
New accounts are offered end-to-end encryption right after signing up: choose a passphrase and save the recovery code somewhere safe, or continue without it and turn it on later.
Choose Install app on the home page or in the account menu to add Catat Saja to your phone or computer. It opens even when you are offline.
Everything saves itself as you type. The "Saving…" and "Saved" status next to the date shows when it is done.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Write anything down: ideas, plans, recipes, minutes.
steps: On the Notes page, choose New note and start typing. Choose Format or right-click for bold text, headings and lists.
Leaving a note keeps it, even if you never pressed Save.
Use the icon bar at the top to pin a note to the top of the list, archive it to tidy your list (it moves to Archived at the bottom, only for you), share it, undo or redo changes, or delete it.
The Gemini menu (the sparkles icon) can summarise a note, tidy it up, translate it between English and Indonesian, or turn it into a new task list.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.description: Checklists for shopping, packing, chores or anything with steps.
steps: On the Tasks page, choose New task, give it a title and type each item in Add item.
Paste several lines at once to add one item per line.
Tap an item to edit it, move it up or down to reorder, and use Check all or Uncheck all for the whole list.
Checked items move to Completed at the bottom. If you remove an item by mistake, undo it from the message that appears.

finances.title: Finances
finances.description: Keep a book for a month, a trip or a project, with income, expenses and the balance.
steps: On the Finances page, choose New book and pick the book's currency.
Choose Add entry for each income or expense: description, amount, quantity, category and date. Amount fields accept sums such as 25000+12000.
Categories are suggested from your own past entries, worked out on your device. You can always change them.
An entry can be in another currency: it keeps the rate you used, so the book's totals never shift. Set your currencies and rates in Settings → Currency.
Add Your accounts (wallets, bank accounts) to check them against the book's balance.
The book shows cash flow, the balance over time and spending by category, as charts or as a table.

Choose Gemini to scan a receipt or use Quick add. Scan receipt reads a photo into entries, and Quick add turns typed text like "lunch 45rb, salary 8jt yesterday" into entries. Both use Gemini, and you check the entries before they are added.

health.title: Health
health.description: Keep a health log for yourself, a child or a parent.
steps: On the Health page, create a log with a name, sex and birth date.
Choose Add measurement to record weight and height (with BMI), blood sugar, uric acid, cholesterol, calories or a period.
For a child, growth is compared with the WHO standards from birth to 19 years, with percentiles and the Kemenkes status.
Results are shown against reference ranges, never as a diagnosis. Ask a doctor about anything that worries you.
Add reminder to be reminded to measure every few days or before an expected period. Due reminders show in the app, and Add to calendar puts them on your phone's calendar.
Settings → Health chooses the adult BMI categories and the units results are shown in.

search.title: Search
search.description: Find anything you wrote, across notes, tasks, finances and health logs.
steps: Use the search box at the top, or press Ctrl K (⌘ K on a Mac) or / from any page.
Search looks at titles and content. Choose See all to filter a list by what you typed.

sharing.title: Sharing
sharing.description: Share any note, task list, finance book or health log with other people who use Catat Saja.
steps: Choose Share in the icon bar, find someone by their email, and give them read-only or edit access. They get an invitation, and the item is added to their list once they accept.

Something shared with you shows as an invitation at the top of your lists and under the bell next to search: Accept to add it to your list, Decline, or Block to also stop that person inviting you (unblock them in Settings → Account).
Changes show up for everyone straight away. People with read-only access can't change anything.
You can copy a link to the item, and undo removing someone.
Something shared with you can be taken off your own list with Remove from my list; it stays for everyone else.

encryption.title: End-to-end encryption
encryption.description: Your items are encrypted on your device, so only you and the people you share with can read them; not even we can.
steps: New accounts can set it up right after signing up. If you skipped it, or your account is older, turn it on in Settings → Account → Security.
Unlock your data on each device with your passphrase, your recovery code, or a passkey (fingerprint, face or device PIN).
Keep your recovery code safe: if you forget your passphrase, it is the only way back into your encrypted items.
Choose Lock this device in the account menu when you are done on a shared computer.

gemini.title: Gemini helpers
gemini.description: Optional helpers that use Google's Gemini: receipt scanning, quick add, dictation, and the note and task list helpers.
steps: The first time you use one, a notice explains what is sent. Nothing is sent until you choose a photo, press a button or stop a recording.
You always see the result first, and nothing is added or changed until you accept it. Gemini's changes can be undone.
Gemini's free tier lets Google use what is sent to improve its services, even for encrypted items, so don't send what you'd rather keep private.
You can stop using Gemini at any time in Settings → Account → AI features.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Open Settings from the account menu (your photo at the top).
steps: General: your name and photo; light, dark or system theme; text size and language; the menu order and the page the app opens on.
Account: your email, linking Google, encryption and passkeys, and the AI features.
Currency: your currencies and their rates, and how amounts are written.
Health: how health results are judged and shown.

privacyPolicy.collect: When you create an account, we store your email address and display name. If you sign in with Google, we also store your Google profile photo. We store the notes, tasks, finance books, health logs and settings you create.
privacyPolicy.use: We use this only to run the app: to sign you in, keep your data and let you share it. We don't sell your data or use it for advertising.
privacyPolicy.storage: Everything is stored with Google Firebase (Authentication and Cloud Firestore) and is covered by Google's security and privacy practices. So the app works offline, each browser you use also keeps a copy of your items (encrypted items stay encrypted) and of an entry you were typing and hadn't saved; for an encrypted book, that draft is kept only until the tab closes. Signing out deletes them from that browser.
privacyPolicy.encryption: With end-to-end encryption (offered when you sign up, and available to everyone in Settings), the content of your notes, tasks, finance books and health logs is encrypted on your device before it is saved, with keys only you and the people you share with hold. We and Google can't read it. What the app needs to work stays readable: who an item belongs to, who it is shared with, when it changed, and how many months a finance book's entries span (never which months). If you lose both your passphrase and your recovery code, nobody can recover your encrypted data.
privacyPolicy.ai: Receipt scanning, quick add, dictation, note helpers and task list helpers are optional. Only when you use one is what you chose sent to Google’s Gemini (through Firebase AI Logic): a receipt photo, the text you typed or pasted, a voice recording you made, or the note’s or task list’s title and text, even for end-to-end encrypted items. Google may keep it and use it to improve its services. We don’t store what is sent; what you add or change is stored like anything else. You agree to this once, before the first use, and can take it back in Settings → Account.
privacyPolicy.sharing: When you share a note, task, book or health log, the people you invite can see its content (their invitation shows its title), and it is added to their lists only if they accept. Others can find you by your exact email address to share with you; they then see your name and photo. Nobody can browse a list of users. If you block someone, they can't invite you any more; your list of blocked people is private and they aren't told.
privacyPolicy.analytics: We use Google Analytics for Firebase to understand how the app is used, for example which pages are opened. It collects usage and device information, never the content of your items.
privacyPolicy.security: To keep out abuse, the app uses Firebase App Check with Google reCAPTCHA, which checks that requests come from this app using signals from your browser.
privacyPolicy.video: The home page has videos hosted on YouTube. They load only when you press play or choose a story, from YouTube's privacy-enhanced mode (youtube-nocookie.com); YouTube's own privacy policy then applies to them.
privacyPolicy.contact: To get a copy of your data, or to delete your account and everything in it, email {{email}}.

medications.empty: No medicines yet. Add one to be reminded at each dose and keep track of what was taken.
medications.hint: Doses waiting to be marked show here, under the bell and on the Health menu. For an alert on time, add a medicine to your phone’s calendar. Always follow your doctor’s or pharmacist’s directions.
medications.toggle: Mark taken, or clear the mark

setup.title: Turn on end-to-end encryption
setup.description: Your notes, lists, books and health logs are encrypted on your device before they're saved. Nobody else can read them: not us, not Google, and not anyone who gets a copy of the database.
setup.passphraseHint: At least 10 characters. Use something you'll remember: nobody can reset it for you.
setup.skipHint: Your items are then protected by your sign-in, but not end-to-end encrypted. You can turn it on any time in Settings → Account → Security.

recovery.title: Save your recovery code
recovery.description: If you forget your passphrase, this code is the only way back into your encrypted data. Keep it somewhere safe, away from this device.
recovery.label: Recovery code
recovery.fileHeading: Catat Saja recovery code. Keep it private and safe.
recovery.confirm: I've saved my recovery code somewhere safe

passkey.title: Unlock with a passkey (optional)
passkey.description: Use your fingerprint, face or device PIN instead of typing your passphrase on this device.

unlock.title: Unlock your data
unlock.description: Enter your passphrase to read your encrypted items on this device. It stays unlocked until you lock it or sign out.
unlock.recoverDescription: Enter your recovery code and choose a new passphrase.
unlock.recover: Unlock and save the new passphrase

settings.title: Security
settings.description: End-to-end encryption is off. Your items are protected by your account and the database rules.
settings.on: End-to-end encryption is on, and this device is unlocked.
settings.howItWorks: Turn on end-to-end encryption so only you, and the people you share with, can read your items. You'll choose a passphrase and get a recovery code.
settings.recoveryDescription: This new code replaces your old one, which stops working.
settings.sharedNote: Items shared with people who haven't turned on encryption stay unencrypted until they do.
settings.unreadable_one: {{count}} of your encrypted items is shared with someone who turned off encryption, so they can't read it.
settings.unreadable_other: {{count}} of your encrypted items are shared with people who turned off encryption, so they can't read them.
settings.sharedPlain: Shared unencrypted: everyone can read them again

share.notSetUp: {{email}} hasn't turned on encryption, so they can't read this encrypted item. Share it without encryption? It will be stored unencrypted for everyone.

off.title: Turn off end-to-end encryption?
off.own: Your encrypted notes, lists, books and health logs will be stored unencrypted again, so we and Google could technically read them. People you share them with keep access. Your passphrase, recovery code and passkeys stop working.
off.fromOthers_one: {{count}} item someone else encrypted and shared with you will no longer be readable for you, until its owner shares it again without encryption.
off.fromOthers_other: {{count}} items others encrypted and shared with you will no longer be readable for you, until their owners share them again without encryption.

notice.title: Use Gemini?
notice.send: What you use it on (a receipt photo, text you type or paste, a voice recording, a note or a task list) is sent to Google’s Gemini to read, write down or rewrite it. Google may keep it and use it to improve its services, so leave out anything you don’t want to share.
notice.encryption: This happens even for end-to-end encrypted items: that content leaves your device, while what you save is encrypted as usual. Catat Saja doesn’t keep what is sent.
notice.check: Nothing is sent until you use one of these features, and you check the result before anything is added or changed. You can take this back in Settings → Account.

maintenance.title: We're updating Catat Saja
maintenance.description: The app is closed for a short while so nothing gets lost while it changes. Your data is safe. This page opens again by itself when we're done.

update.title: A new version is ready
update.description: Catat Saja has changed how it stores your data. Reload to keep going with the new version; what you saved is safe.

toast.archived: Archived. Find it under Archived at the bottom of the list.

block.hint: Decline, and stop this person inviting you. You can unblock them in Settings → Account.

toast.blocked: Blocked. They can’t invite you any more.
toast.unblocked: Unblocked. They can invite you again.

settings.title: Blocked people
settings.description: People you blocked can’t invite you to anything. They aren’t told that you blocked them.

update.title: New version
update.description: A newer version of Catat Saja is available. Reload to use it; what you saved is safe.
